newsitems.title: Dev Blog 1: What You Build Stays Built
newsitems.author: Sulfurr` (CM Verse Project)
newsitems.contents: Hello, Spacemen!Starting with this post, we're moving to a new format for our updates. Instead of dense patch notes, we'll be sharing smaller, more regular dev diaries - picking a couple of things we're working on and telling you the story behind them in more detail.This time, we want to walk you through two things that shape what it actually means to live and work in the Verse universe.🏗 Every Resource You Deliver Goes Somewhere RealVerse starts at a very specific point in history - humanity has barely stabilized the Earth-Moon system. The infrastructure exists, but just barely. Everything beyond that doesn't, and none of it appears on its own.Every resource you mine and deliver goes somewhere real. The system tracks exactly what's been contributed, and toward what. When enough has come in to push a construction goal forward, it moves forward. When it hasn't, it waits.That means early players are laying literal groundwork. The first infrastructure milestones will carry the contributions of whoever was there when it happened, and we intend to make those marks permanent. Later players will have plenty to do, but they won't be able to do this🌚 What the Kessler Belt Means for Everyday LifeThe Kessler Belt isn't just the reason you can't freely land on Earth. It's one of the forces shaping daily life on Host Station.Earth is still there. It still sends people, culture, electronics, biological goods, familiar comforts - but every shipment has to pass through a narrow, constantly maintained corridor cutting through a dangerous debris field. That changes what ordinary things are worth.An Earth-grown product isn't necessarily rare where it came from. On Host Station, its price includes launch capacity, corridor maintenance, protected transport, insurance, and the risk that the next shipment gets delayed entirely. We want the economy to reflect that - goods should tell you where they came from and what it cost to get them here.So here's a question for you: what Earth-side goods would feel meaningful to you as expensive orbital imports? Fresh food, medicine, physical media, luxury materials, or something you wouldn't expect?If you're into this kind of behind-the-scenes look at how Verse is built, or just want project news more often than we post it here, our Discord, Reddit and Twitter are the places to be:\Discord] \Reddit] \Twitter/X]

newsitems.title: Holiday Test Client Update
newsitems.author: Kai-3
newsitems.contents: ✨ Happy New Year, Spacers! ✨The Verse Project team would like to wish you a Happy New Year!Thank you for spending this year with us — exploring, testing, sharing ideas, and helping shape the Verse universe step by step. Your feedback and support mean a lot to us and help guide the project forward.The start of a new year is a moment to look back, let go of what no longer matters, and set new courses. We are truly glad to walk this path together with you and believe that many more discoveries lie ahead.---🎁 Holiday Test Client UpdateTo celebrate the holidays, we’ve released an update for the test game client, which includes:• Early version of the starting tutorial The first step toward the future missions and quest system.• New settings options Including motion blur toggle and inverted controls.• Station hub improvements Updates and visual improvements to the main hall environment.• Stability improvements Fixes for several crashes and overall client stability improvements.• Partial localization Support for several languages has been added, with more coming in future updates.---🚀 What’s Coming NextWe’re actively working on the next updates for Verse. Here’s a glimpse of what’s ahead:• New procedural celestial body generation Featuring a real-time foliage subsystem that places rocks, terrain elements, and vegetation directly on planetary surfaces.• New station areas Including a dedicated character spawn space to replace the current fixed spawn point in the hub.• New ships Another shuttle-class ship is nearly ready, and development continues on the first multi-crew ship designed for cooperative gameplay and shared roles.---✨ May the coming year bring you calm, inspiration, and the strength to keep moving forward — both in the game and beyond.Thank you for staying with us and helping make this universe feel alive.Happy New Year, and see you among the stars! 🚀 — The Verse Project Team

newsitems.title: Stage IV: Update Available
newsitems.author: Synthes Games
newsitems.contents: 🫡 Hello, Spacemen! The Verse Project team is excited to introduce a new update for our technical demo. Yes, this is finally Stage IV! However, this time, we have significantly deviated from our initial plans to focus more on important aspects. We have concentrated on performance, network code optimization, orbital flights, and combat systems. We hope this will add more variety to the gameplay experience, even at this early stage of development, and pave the way for new features in the near future. 🚨 Remember: the technical demo is not a full-fledged game with complete gameplay, graphics, and visual effects. It is merely a demonstration of our capabilities and may contain various issues and bugs. {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45280868/ec81bd8b7551a23a14ecb522b57cdce68ee096ac.jpg 📋 What's New? 🪐 Orbital Flight We've lifted the restriction on flying only near the station—now you can embark on a journey around the Moon. However, you cannot fly closer than 80 km to the surface or farther than 100,000 km. Landing has been postponed for future updates to allow us to refine this feature. You now have access to a fully free orbital flight mode, where you can move with or without the flight assistant enabled. For this update, we have significantly increased the power of ship engines to make space travel a bit easier. This is a temporary measure, as we need to thoroughly test the world compositor under orbital speed conditions and make the gameplay more accessible until we implement all the necessary navigation tools. 🛰️ Orbital Objects The starting station, where your journey begins, now moves in orbit around the Moon. Yes, in previous versions, it was stationary. Additionally, we have added several orbital objects that you can find and visit. Two of them are easily located in the ship's navigation panel (on the left); they can be selected as targets, so you will always know their positions. The others remain hidden—they have no navigation markers, but they can still be discovered and visited. 🔫 Close-Range Combat You can now activate ship weapons and fire at close-range targets. Each of the three available ships has its own course weapons with unique characteristics. You can test each one in battle against other players. To add some variety, we've introduced the Outlaw Roster, where you can see the list of the most successful players. For now, the list updates only after a server restart (usually once a day). 🌚 Celestial Body Generation The procedural generation of massive orbital objects has been significantly improved. You will notice this when looking at the Moon—performance has been enhanced, and landscape variety has increased. Although landing is not yet possible, some surface details can already be seen from low orbit. This is far from a complete list of everything we've worked on. You can experience all the new features firsthand in the demo build available on our website. Don't forget to share your thoughts in our Discord server—the Verse Project team will be happy to hear your feedback! If you encounter any issues or bugs, please report them in the ⁠🆘〢support channel in our discord or in the Steam community. Thank you for your support! 🚀

newsitems.title: Stage III Update Available
newsitems.author: Synthes Games
newsitems.contents: 🫡 Hello, Spaceman! o7 We’re a bit late this time, as we needed to spend extra time on polishing, optimizations, and additional adjustments. The main goal of this update is to create truly large orbital structures that you can freely move around. This approach was chosen from the beginning to lay the groundwork for a variety of objects in space and on planetary surfaces. The project demo is available on the project website. This will be available on Steam at a later date. 🚨 The tech demo is not a game with full gameplay, graphics and visual effects. It is only a demonstration of our features. Here’s a brief list of what’s included in this update: Station Exterior Our first space station, HOST, which you’ve already seen from the inside, has received significant upgrades and added exterior details. This is not the final implementation, and we’ll continue to improve model and texture detail as our development tools advance. Ship Flights In this update, you can now fly beyond the station on ships and return by requesting docking permission from the left navigation panel. The current flight model has limited functionality, and the free movement zone is limited to 10 km around the station. By default, each ship has a flight assist mode that helps control the ship and limits its speed. If desired, the assist can be turned off with the B key. Sound Environment Our team has made substantial improvements to the project’s sound design. Many objects now have new sounds that were previously missing. Ships, engines, and various station structures are now partially voiced. We’re continuing to experiment in this area to further enhance the soundscape. Visual Effects The effects for ships’ main and maneuvering thrusters have been reworked to better match the original concept. Particle effects around the moving ship have also been added. Known Issues In some cases, the elevator may move into open space when entered. Elevator shaft doors may fail to close. Significant FPS drops can occur inside a moving ship if you’re not seated in the pilot’s chair. Position synchronization over distances of several kilometers from the station may have inaccuracies. Object collisions may be inaccurate, potentially allowing the ship to partially pass through them. 🚨 Multiplayer bandwidth is also limited and will change as testing progresses. For reporting bugs and issues, you can use the related thread in the discussions or project discord server.
